# Deploy manifests do not cover the host disk-cap scripts

## What

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`'s `*_PATHS` manifests do not list either of the ADR 0112 host
cap scripts:

- `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` (story `9183-aaae-667d-45e6`)
- `infra/scripts/journald-cap.sh` (story `e956-b1c3-45b9-4016`)

Both are consumed by `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (`--print-env`, and for journald
`--check-active`) and installed by `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` (`--install`). Those two
CONSUMERS are covered — `observability.sh` by `OBS_PATHS`, `compose-up.sh` by
`MATERIALIZER_PATHS` — but the cap scripts themselves are in neither.

## Consequence

A commit that changes ONLY a cap value (the exact edit ADR 0112 decision 6 says an operator
should be able to make) changes no path in any manifest, so autodeploy signals nothing and the
new ceiling is not applied until some unrelated change happens to trigger the same action. The
files themselves do reach the box with the checkout, so this is a missed TRIGGER rather than a
missing file — but it is the drift class `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` exists for.

`check_deploy_manifest.py` does not catch it: it derives its expected path set from
Dockerfile/compose references and from filename conventions (`materialize-*.sh`,
`*-entrypoint.sh`, `compose-up.sh`), and `*-cap.sh` matches none of them.

## Why this is not fixed inside either story

Editing `autodeploy.sh` was outside both stories' declared `file_impact`, and adding a path
there invalidates a signed plan-review attestation whose currency basis IS the file impact.
The gap is shared by both scripts, so it is one change here rather than half a change in each.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both cap scripts are listed in the manifests whose actions actually consume them, or an
      in-tree comment records why a given manifest deliberately excludes them.
- [ ] `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` derives `infra/**/*-cap.sh` (or an equivalent rule)
      so a future host-cap script cannot be added without manifest coverage.
- [ ] A test proves the new derivation is non-vacuous: removing a cap script from the manifests
      fails the gate.
